title: Account, Profile, Security and Privacy pages
summary: Self-service settings split into Account, Profile, Security and Privacy for public and staff accounts, with old /profile URLs redirecting.
changes: Authenticated settings use /account, /account/profile, /account/security and /account/privacy with shared sub-navigation; /profile and its hash anchors redirect to the matching page.
Account holds username, email change, sign-in summary and appearance; Profile holds personal and contact details (including date of birth with step-up when it changes).
Security holds password, passkeys, two-factor authentication, telephone PIN, signed-in devices with sign-out of other sessions, and recent security activity.

Privacy holds contact and email preferences (with policy-version audits), cookie choices, push notification settings (moved from Profile), download of your own data, and a deletion request that opens an APES CIC case.

Staff use the same four pages: directory identity is read-only on Account, workplace fields stay on Profile, and Security offers passkeys and PIN with Cloudron links where the directory owns password and 2FA.
Help, wiki and in-app guides describe the four pages; user menu and quick actions point at Account.
affected_areas: Account settings routes and user menu
Privacy preferences, notifications, data export and deletion
version_rationale: MINOR: splits the single profile page into four self-service areas and adds sessions, export and deletion request without removing existing accounts.
validation: PHPUnit AccountSettingsRoutesTest, AccountProfilePersonalDetailsTest, AccountSecurityPageTest, AccountPrivacyPageTest, StaffProfileWorkflowTest and a 491-test account/security/privacy filter.
Herd preview at https://myapes-account.test for Account settings pages.

known_limitations: Staff managing other people's accounts remains out of scope (later version).
Admin security policy remains out of scope (later version).
Design-QA profile screenshots still show the pre-split single page and are labelled as historical.
